name: Prevalon Energy
ownership: subsidiary (Nextpower, formerly Nextracker — acquisition completed July 20, 2026)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Prevalon is the US mid-tier BESS integrator moving hardest at the AI-data-center power problem — a Mitsubishi Power Americas spinout (Feb 2024) that built a purpose-built Hybrid Power Stabilizer for GPU load swings, holds 1.3 GW of firm supply contracts it says are exclusively for hyperscaler data-center projects, and pivoted its cell supply from Chinese sources to US-made AESC cells via Fixx Energy's Tennessee plant — before being acquired by Nextpower (formerly Nextracker) for up to $365M, completed 20 July 2026. BACKGROUND: The company launched with Mitsubishi Power's entire energy-storage team, technology and ~3 GWh of installed base; an April 2024 restructuring made it a joint venture of Mitsubishi Power Americas and EES (management plus outside investors), and CEO Tom Cornell set a target of a $1B business within five years. Current company-claimed scale: 35+ projects, 6.4+ GWh deployed globally, 6+ GWh under long-term service agreements. Flagship delivered work runs through Idaho Power (80 MW/320 MWh at COD June 2025, plus a 200 MW/800 MWh follow-on for 2026), an unnamed 600 MWh Western US utility, SDG&E microgrids, and Chilean projects with Innergex. Revenue and headcount have never been disclosed; the $365M cash-and-stock price with gross-profit-linked earnouts through 2030 is the best public marker of its size.
ecosystemRole: We assess Prevalon as the clearest example of a Western mid-tier integrator converting the FEOC regime from threat into positioning: it ran on Chinese REPT cells and a Chinese contract manufacturer (CLOU), then moved first among its peers to lock 10 GWh of US-made AESC cells through Fixx Energy's Tennessee plant — the same domestic-cell route Fluence uses — while wrapping the offer in a US-built, IEC 62443-certified EMS and Mitsubishi heavy-power heritage. For the AIDC ecosystem its significance is the Hybrid Power Stabilizer: a BESS-plus-power-electronics product aimed at the same GPU load-swing problem NVIDIA's 800 VDC papers assign to rack capacitors and facility BESS, tested against hyperscaler load profiles at a US DOE national laboratory. Under Nextpower ownership it becomes the storage arm of an integrated tracker-eBOS-PCS-BESS platform explicitly aimed at AI data-center power — a Fluence-shaped competitor with a solar-hardware distribution machine behind it.

productsAndServices.name: HD5 DC (modular liquid-cooled DC block)
productsAndServices.description: Current-generation 5 MWh-per-20-ft-enclosure DC LFP platform: 360 MWh/acre site density, 2-8 hour durations, 8,000+ full cycles, 20+ year design life. Certifications listed: UL 1973, UL 9540, UL 9540A ed.4, UL 1741, IEEE 1547, IEEE 693 (seismic), UN 38.3, NFPA 855/70/69. CSA TS-800 large-scale fire test completed April 2025 with contract manufacturer CLOU — full unit burn in a four-unit back-to-back array, fire contained to the single unit.
productsAndServices.positioning: Mid-scale challenger to Megapack/PowerTitan-class blocks on safety validation, seismic qualification and (post-AESC deal) domestic content rather than on cost or volume — Prevalon is absent from Wood Mackenzie's 2026 global top-10.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to utilities and IPPs as supply-plus-integration, almost always bundled with a long-term service agreement
productsAndServices.roadmap: US-manufactured AESC cell/module content phasing in from the June 2026 Fixx/AESC 10 GWh agreement; Nextpower's Zigor/Apex PCS intended to come in-house

productsAndServices.name: HD5 AC (integrated AC block, May 2026)
productsAndServices.description: Fully integrated AC block: 5 MWh per enclosure (25°C), 2/4/8-hour configurations, up to 426 MWh/acre, round-trip efficiency up to 92.5% (4-hour), >8,000 cycles to 65% SOH, 20-year rated life. Distributed 500 kW string PCS blocks integrated in-enclosure with a single point of common coupling, direct MV-transformer connection (eliminating the 1,500 Vdc collection layer and separate 480 Vac auxiliary feed), self-powered chillers, battery-powered commissioning, and a claimed up-to-10x reduction in short-circuit current for arc-flash safety.
productsAndServices.positioning: The AC-block integration play — competes with Tesla Megapack 3/Megablock and Wartsila Quantum3 on engineering integration rather than scale; PCS vendor undisclosed pending the Nextpower Zigor/Apex fit.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to utilities and IPPs; supply extended to US, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand facilities for US-bound product, with China supply retained for non-US markets
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale front-of-meter storage; data-center campus storage

productsAndServices.name: Hybrid Power Stabilizer (HPS) for data centers (Feb 2026)
productsAndServices.description: BESS-plus-power-electronics architecture purpose-built for AI data centers: absorbs GPU-driven load swings, stabilizes voltage and frequency, bridges grid, islanded and on-site-generation modes, and carries UPS-replacement ambitions. Coordinates gas turbines, reciprocating engines, fuel cells, grid and renewables under the insightOS EMS. Hardware-in-the-loop testing announced April 2026 at a US DOE national laboratory covering GPU load variability, loss of load/generation, faults and islanded architectures.
productsAndServices.positioning: The most explicit AIDC-native storage product from any US mid-tier integrator — the Mitsubishi gas-turbine heritage shows in the multi-source coordination; 1.3 GW of firm hyperscaler-exclusive supply contracts claimed at launch, first deliveries from 2026.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to hyperscalers and AI-campus developers; six projects in development, two fully released at announcement
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscale and colocation data centers, AI campuses with hybrid generation
productsAndServices.roadmap: CEO projects revenue mix moving from ~80% utility-scale to 50/50 in 2026 and potentially 75% data-center within several years

productsAndServices.name: insightOS EMS (Mar 2025)
productsAndServices.description: US-designed and US-built energy management system: IEC 62443-4-1 certified, NERC CIP and NIST 800-53 alignment claimed, MESA standards; plant-level control, grid-forming, black start, islanding, millisecond-class response.
productsAndServices.positioning: The cyber-provenance counter to Chinese-EMS scrutiny — sold as the control layer for utilities and security-sensitive data-center buyers.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with HD5 and HPS systems
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utilities with NERC CIP obligations; data-center operators
productsAndServices.roadmap: Extends across Nextpower's combined storage-and-PCS platform

productsAndServices.name: Long-term services and customer financing
productsAndServices.description: 6+ GWh under long-term service agreements (10-year LTSAs standard on utility projects); $250M customer financing programme (Deferral Payment Program) launched September 2025 with J.P. Morgan Payments.
productsAndServices.positioning: The service book is the recurring-revenue franchise and the bankability proof point for a company that publishes no financials.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Earnout RSUs tied to gross-profit targets through 2030 imply service-margin focus under Nextpower

recentDevelopments.headline: Nextpower completes the Prevalon acquisition — up to $365M in cash and stock, with 810,733 performance RSUs vesting 2026-2030 on Prevalon gross-profit targets plus up to 375,000 service RSUs; Tom Cornell continues to lead the business
recentDevelopments.read: The third ownership structure in thirty months lands Prevalon inside a NASDAQ-listed platform whose stated rationale is AI data-center power supply — the balance-sheet question that shadowed a private JV is answered, at the cost of the Mitsubishi halo.

recentDevelopments.headline: AESC signs a multi-year, 10 GWh cell and module supply agreement with Prevalon — including US-manufactured, domestic-content modules via Fixx Energy, which took control of AESC's Smyrna, Tennessee LFP plant on April 1, 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The FEOC pivot made concrete: Prevalon swaps Chinese REPT cells for the same Tennessee domestic-cell route Fluence uses, making the Smyrna plant shared ground between the two most FEOC-forward Western integrators.

recentDevelopments.headline: Nextpower announces a definitive agreement to acquire Prevalon for up to $365M; raises FY27 outlook to $4.0-4.4B revenue and $845-930M adjusted EBITDA
recentDevelopments.read: Dan Shugar buys the team after customer references — pairing Prevalon with the Zigor/Apex PCS acquisitions gives Nextpower an in-house PCS-BESS-EMS stack aimed at AI data centers.

recentDevelopments.headline: HD5 AC launched: 5 MWh integrated AC block, up to 426 MWh/acre, 92.5% RTE (4-hour), distributed 500 kW string PCS, direct MV connection
recentDevelopments.read: The AC-block move matches where Tesla (Megablock) and Wartsila (Quantum3) are taking the market — integration engineering as the differentiator for a player that cannot win on volume.

recentDevelopments.headline: HPS hardware-in-the-loop testing announced at a US DOE national laboratory, covering GPU/accelerator load variability, loss-of-load events, faults and islanded architectures, with hyperscalers participating
recentDevelopments.read: Third-party lab validation is precisely what a newly launched data-center product needs to clear hyperscaler technical review — the testing scope reads like the NVIDIA 800 VDC papers' problem list.

recentDevelopments.headline: Hybrid Power Stabilizer for data centers launched; ~1.3 GW already contracted with hyperscale customers, first deliveries from 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The most explicit AIDC storage product from any US mid-tier integrator — and the 1.3 GW claim, if real, is a larger data-center book than any competitor has disclosed.

recentDevelopments.headline: CEO Cornell details the FEOC response: buyers now scrutinise origin, ownership and control; supply diversified to US, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand facilities; long-lead equipment pre-bought under multiple sourcing scenarios
recentDevelopments.read: An unusually candid public account of how a mid-tier integrator re-plumbed its supply chain around the January 2026 FEOC and Section 301 changes.

recentDevelopments.headline: Global collaboration with Emerson: HD5 and insightOS integrated with Emerson's Ovation automation platform for hyperscale, colocation and enterprise data centers
recentDevelopments.read: Ovation is incumbent in power-plant control rooms — the tie-up routes Prevalon into data-center power procurement through an automation vendor operators already trust.

recentDevelopments.headline: $250M customer financing programme (Deferral Payment Program) launched with J.P. Morgan Payments
recentDevelopments.read: Vendor financing is a bankability instrument — it substitutes for the Mitsubishi balance sheet the spinout progressively left behind.

recentDevelopments.headline: Happy Valley (Idaho Power) reaches commercial operation: 80 MW/320 MWh, 4-hour, with long-term service agreement
recentDevelopments.read: The reference COD for the regulated-utility franchise; the 200 MW/800 MWh follow-on contracted January 2025 targets 2026 operation.

recentDevelopments.headline: CSA TS-800 large-scale fire test completed with contract manufacturer CLOU: full unit burn in a four-unit array with no propagation
recentDevelopments.read: Safety validation at array level — the test configuration (back-to-back, side-by-side) mirrors real site layouts rather than isolated-unit burns.

recentDevelopments.headline: Second Idaho Power contract: 200 MW/800 MWh, 4-hour, with LTSA, COD targeted 2026
recentDevelopments.read: Repeat business from a regulated utility is the strongest reference class in US storage — Idaho Power plans ~1,100 MW of 4-hour storage for its 2045 clean-energy requirement.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Prevalon's differentiation as provenance engineering rather than product scale: US-built IEC 62443-certified controls, CSA large-scale fire testing, IEEE 693 seismic qualification, and — since June 2026 — US-made AESC cells through Fixx Energy's Tennessee plant. Basis: the certification stack on the HD5 datasheets, the Fixx/AESC 10 GWh agreement, and the company's absence from every volume ranking — it cannot be selling on cost.

(High confidence) We assess the AIDC pivot as the company's defining bet. Basis: a purpose-built product (HPS), DOE-laboratory validation against GPU load profiles, the Emerson Ovation integration, a claimed 1.3 GW hyperscaler-exclusive contract book, and the CEO's own projection of a 50/50 utility/data-center revenue mix in 2026 moving toward 75% data-center. The Nextpower acquisition rationale names AI data-center power supply explicitly.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the FEOC pivot as genuine but incomplete: the REPT/CLOU Chinese supply history is recent, the Fixx-controlled Smyrna plant changed hands only in April 2026 and is shared with Fluence, and whether Envision's continuing licence role in that plant survives Treasury's final FEOC regulations is an open legal question. A domestic-content claim built on Smyrna cells carries regulatory tail risk that Prevalon does not control.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Nextpower acquisition as solving Prevalon's two structural weaknesses — balance sheet and channel — while creating a retention problem. The earnout structure (performance RSUs through 2030) is designed to hold the ex-Mitsubishi team, but three ownership structures in thirty months is a real concern for counterparties signing 20-year service agreements.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the 1.3 GW hyperscaler contract book as the single most important unverified number in the profile: no customer is named, no third party has corroborated it, and the company's own website conflates prior project execution with HPS-specific deployment. If it is real, Prevalon has quietly built the largest disclosed data-center storage book of any integrator; if it is inflated, the AIDC story is a product launch plus a DOE test.
